headline: Morning stabilization keeps Tail low while yields, oil and Hormuz disruption sustain extreme Stress
body: Latest verified morning evidence shows firmer Nasdaq futures and broadly positive technology breadth, while the U.S. 10-year yield remains near 4.71% and Brent near $94. Strait of Hormuz traffic remains severely constrained. No persistent one-way NQ structure with failed retracements is independently verified.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock hours, Tail rose from low morning readings into WATCH/BLOCK during Thursday's U.S. selloff, peaked at 29% late in the session, then decayed overnight as futures stabilized and current Tail returned to the low band.
outlookSummary: Risk is concentrated around 15:25–16:30 Berlin for the U.S. cash open and state-employment release. Conditional Tail peaks at 24% and remains below the block threshold unless persistent one-way structure with weak retracements is observed; after Friday's futures close, risk shifts toward weekend headline and reopening-gap uncertainty.

forecast.analysis: Latest verified morning evidence is constructive but not one-way: Nasdaq futures were higher, while the 10-year yield stayed near 4.71% and Brent near $94. Fresh breadth context is positive, but no persistent NQ extension with failed retracements is independently verified.

forecast.analysis: European morning trade is a retracement-quality checkpoint. Tail stays low if firmer technology breadth coexists with two-sided index trade; synchronized yield and oil pressure with renewed downside extension would raise conditional risk.

Late European morning shifts focus toward U.S. premarket liquidity. Conditional Tail remains low unless NQ begins holding near downside extremes while megacaps, semiconductors and yields align against equities.

Approaching the U.S. opening sequence lifts conditional Tail into WATCH. Direction is unobserved; the key checkpoint is whether pre-open structure becomes persistently one-way rather than merely volatile.

The U.S. cash open is imminent. Thursday's weak close and still-elevated yields increase conditional continuation risk, but a block would require observed opening extension with poor retracement quality.

First-hour cash price discovery overlaps the 16:00 Berlin state labor release. Tail peaks at WATCH; only observed persistent extension with shallow or failed retracements would justify crossing the block threshold.

Post-release price discovery remains conditionally elevated. Tail would fall if the opening move retraces meaningfully and breadth stabilizes; repeated extension after failed rebounds would keep risk near the threshold.
Late-morning U.S. trade is a normalization checkpoint. Two-sided price action and easing cross-asset pressure would reduce Tail; renewed index extension with weak rebounds would delay the decay.
Midday liquidity usually lowers directional efficiency. Tail returns to the low band conditionally if NQ is not pinned near session extremes and volatility does not re-accelerate.
Early afternoon remains a monitoring hour rather than a scheduled-event window. Conditional Tail stays low if breadth is balanced and the morning range is not extending persistently.
The U.S. power-hour approach raises conditional Tail modestly. A late-session continuation becomes more relevant only if NQ is already holding near an extreme with shallow pullbacks.
Cash-close price discovery can amplify an existing trend, but the forecast remains below block absent observed late-session extension. Orderly closing trade would keep Tail in the low band.
After the Friday futures close, live NQ path evidence is unavailable. Tail reflects weekend gap and headline uncertainty rather than an observed directional path.
Weekend conditions remove continuous NQ price discovery. Geopolitical headlines can affect reopening-gap risk, but cannot be counted as observed one-way market structure before futures reopen.
With futures closed, Tail remains low and Stress stays high from oil, yields and geopolitical uncertainty. Any future reopening reaction remains unobserved and conditional.
No live NQ structure is available during the weekend closure. The forecast therefore separates persistent macro Stress from Tail, which requires an observed price path.
Weekend headline risk persists, but no future directional reaction is assumed. Tail remains low until live price discovery can confirm or reject a gap-and-continuation scenario.
The closed-market interval keeps confidence high in the distinction between Stress and Tail: oil and geopolitical pressure remain material, while path-dependent Tail evidence is unavailable.
During the weekend closure, persistent drivers remain elevated but cannot establish failed mean reversion. Any escalation would be evaluated only after tradable price discovery resumes.
No scheduled U.S. macro release falls in this closed-market hour. Tail remains low because current evidence cannot show one-way extension while NQ is not trading.
Weekend conditions continue to separate headline risk from price-path risk. The forecast does not assume that elevated oil or geopolitical tension will produce a directional Nasdaq gap.
The market remains closed, so Tail stays low absent observed price structure. Stress remains extreme enough to preserve reopening sensitivity if new material headlines emerge.
Closed-market conditions persist. No future move is treated as observed; the next meaningful Tail reassessment requires live NQ price discovery after the weekend.
The 24-hour horizon ends during the weekend closure. Tail remains low because no tradable path can confirm persistent extension; oil, yields and geopolitics continue to dominate Stress.
